units.passage: Permitted, Restricted, and Prohibited Uses – General Purposes Allowed (with human oversight and disclosure) Brainstorming and outlining Grammar, translation, and accessibility support (with verification) Administrative efficiency (e.g., summarization, scheduling) Restricted (requires approval/secure tools) Handling of sensitive data (FERPA/PII/PHI, research data) Automated decision-making in admissions, grading, HR, or financial processes (must include human review) Prohibited Uploading University sensitive data to unapproved AI tools Fabricating or falsifying data, citations, or sources Misrepresenting AI-generated work as entirely one’s own when prohibited Using AI to create harmful, discriminatory, or illegal content Academic Use of AI Faculty should clearly define their AI usage policy in each course syllabus.

units.passage: the use of generative AI in their courses. Faculty are responsible for communicating how AI may foster the achievement of course learning outcomes or inhibit the achievement of those outcomes in their courses. For the sake of clarity, it is strongly recommended that all course syllabi include an AI policy. Expectations should clarify what uses are permitted or prohibited, what documentation, citation, or disclosure is required, and how these boundaries support student learning. When expectations vary across graded activities, faculty are encouraged to use the TTU AI Use Levels (see below) to communicate those differences clearly. Definition of Generative AI and General Policies For purposes of these statements, generative AI refers to tools or embedded features that create or transform text, images, audio, video, code, calculations, data analyses, or other content in response to prompts or user inputs. Basic grammar, spelling, and punctuation features are permitted unless they generate or substantially rewrite content or replace the skill being assessed. Approved assistive technologies and disability accommodations remain available as authorized. Grading with AI At this time, the use of generative AI for grading is not approved at Texas Tech University
units.why: 'the use of generative AI for grading is not approved at Texas Tech University' bars AI from grading student work, which is P46 (humans assign grades); the restriction binds instructors.
units.fit_note: Framed as 'not approved at this time' rather than a permanent ban.
